name: Lymow One / Lymow One Plus 10A
description: A tank-tread (not wheeled) robotic mower from Lymow, a startup founded by former SharkNinja robot-vacuum engineers. Originally crowdfunded on Kickstarter, now shipping commercially. Wire-free RTK-GNSS + camera navigation, claimed 45°/100% slope capability.

specs.label: Drive
specs.note: not wheels — unusual for this category

specs.label: Cutting
specs.note: 1.2–4.0 in height, dual SK5 steel blades

specs.label: Subscription
specs.note: Local RTK base station included; maker confirms no mandatory fees

sourcing: Verified against Lymow's own official site and Kickstarter page, plus independent hands-on reviews from Tom's Guide and PCWorld, and coverage from New Atlas, Yanko Design, Notebookcheck, and PR Newswire. Lymow is a young company (founded 2022) that moved from crowdfunding to commercial retail — company-reported unit-shipped figures are self-reported and unverified. Pricing varies by source and appears promo-dependent. A cutting-width discrepancy exists between the CES 2024 press preview (21 in) and the shipped spec sheet (16 in). Claimed max slope (45°/100%) exceeds what independent testers actually observed (~30°).

pricing.summary: Pricing is fluid and promo-dependent: Lymow's own site lists the One Plus around **$2,799 (10A charger) / $2,599 (5A charger)** on sale against a regular price of $3,199/$2,999, while other outlets cite anywhere from $2,699 to $3,199. Treat any single figure as a snapshot rather than a fixed MSRP.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: The tank-tread drive is Lymow One's defining feature, built for rough, sloped terrain. Obstacle avoidance combines an AI camera (claimed 25+ object types) with 5 ultrasonic sensors and 2 Hall sensors. A CES 2024 press release cited a 21-inch cutting width, but the shipped spec sheet lists 16 inches — an unresolved discrepancy between early marketing and the production unit.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Lymow advertises a maximum climbing slope of 45° (100% grade) for the One/One Plus, but independent hands-on testing from Tom's Guide and PCWorld found it actually manages slopes of roughly 30° — a real gap between the marketed spec and tested performance. Its rubber tank-tread drive is independently confirmed as the genuine differentiator behind that traction.

firmwareCommunity.note: Lymow One / Lymow One Plus 10A has not released a public SDK, firmware repo, or developer API. Not currently listed in Builds & Mods.
